model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; earnings after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock at carrying value (senior to common; flows are pre-preferred-dividend)
equity_bridge.note: us-gaap:PreferredStockValue 30 Jun 2026: 13,028 (15,153 at 31 Dec 2025 after redemptions in H1-2026). Preferred dividends FY2025 876, H1-2026 456; deducting the stock at par rather than the dividends from the flows is equivalent and keeps the engine's tax line clean.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is net income applicable to common shareholders (already after share-based compensation, which is inside compensation expense): FY2020 8,915; FY2021 21,151; FY2022 10,764; FY2023 7,907; FY2024 13,525; FY2025 16,300 (us-gaap:NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic). The 5-year CAGR is from the FY2020 COVID-provision year and the 3-year from the FY2022 post-peak year; measured from the FY2021 peak the 4-year CAGR is -6.3%. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) is negative in four of the last six years and describes nothing. Revenue = net revenues: FY2020 44,560; FY2022 47,365; FY2025 58,283. Equity = total shareholders' equity incl. preferred (CSV); common equity 5-year CAGR is 5.3% (84,729 -> 109,819).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case FY2025 -> FY2036 net-revenue CAGR (58,283 -> 89,217, 3.9%/yr), which is the mid-cycle path: it sits between the 5-year CAGR (5.5%), the 3-year (7.2%, flattered by the FY2022 base) and the peak-to-trough-adjusted -0.4% from FY2021, and it embeds a -5% FY2027 normalisation from the record FY2026 base. Equity CAGR is not used: book value is held down by design (FY2021-25 distributions ran at ~100% of earnings to common).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (5.4%) diverges >30% from EPS (15.8%) and 3-year equity (2.2%) from revenue (7.2%): GS distributes ~100% of earnings through buybacks and dividends, so book value growth does not describe earnings power; EPS CAGRs are also amplified by the 4%/yr share-count shrink and measured from trough-ish bases (FY2020, FY2022). None of the trailing CAGRs is a clean forward proxy for a business whose revenue swung -20% (FY2022) and +27% (H1-2026) around a ~4-5% peak-to-peak trend.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle: FY2026 is a record year and the model does not compound from it. Net revenues fall 5% in FY2027 and are flat in FY2028, then grow ~4% tapering to 2.5% as alternatives, private credit and financing offset the cyclicality of IB and markets. Pre-tax margin settles at 33-34.5% (FY2019-25 average 32.3%), tax 21%, ~15-20% of earnings retained to fund RWA growth with the rest distributed, all capitalised at a 10.5% USD cost of equity. Implies a mid-cycle ROTE of ~16-17% and a fair P/TBV of ~1.8-2.0x.
scenario_narratives.bull: The capital-markets upcycle is structural rather than cyclical: AI-infrastructure financing, a permissive M&A regime and the Basel III recalibration keep Global Banking & Markets at record levels while Goldman Sachs Alternatives and private credit scale to management's 2029 targets. Revenue grows 5-6% through the decade, pre-tax margin holds at 39-40% (near the FY2021 peak), ROTE ~22%. This is roughly what the market price already discounts.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2022-23 style reversal: FY2027 net revenues -15% and FY2028 -5% as the IPO window, AI-capex financing and M&A slow together; pre-tax margin drops to 24-26% on sticky non-comp expense and rising private-credit/card provisions; final Basel III / FRTB rules come in tougher than the March 2026 re-proposal, so capital is retained rather than released through the downturn and the recovered margin is capped at ~31%. Revenue only regains the FY2026 level by FY2036.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a bank on the cash it can distribute to common shareholders after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity -- never on operating cash flow, EBITDA or an enterprise value less net debt, none of which exist in a usable form for a G-SIB. Anchor on a mid-cycle margin rather than the record year, charge share-based compensation as the real expense it is (inside comp), hold the share count flat so buybacks are not counted twice, and deduct the preferred stock as the senior claim. The valuation asks what a permanent owner earns; the market's ~2.8x tangible book is a bet that FY2026's ~23% ROTE is the new normal.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cyclical peak in the anchor year: H1-2026 net revenues were +27% YoY with records in Equities and debt underwriting; the base already normalises FY2027 down 5%, but a FY2022-style -20% would take the value toward the bear case
Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of sustained pre-tax margin is worth roughly $20-25/share; the model's 33-34.5% sits above the FY2019-25 average and below the FY2024-26 run-rate

Retention assumption: if final Basel III / FRTB rules land harsher than the March 2026 re-proposal, or the G-SIB surcharge rises, more than 1.3x g of revenue growth must be retained and distributable cash falls
Private credit growth toward $300bn by 2029 adds a less liquid, credit-sensitive book whose losses have not been tested through a cycle
Cost of equity: at 9.5% instead of 10.5% the base value rises ~15%; at 11.5% it falls ~12%; the single 10.5% rate carries no scenario-specific premium
Goodwill and intangibles rose ~$2.5bn in H1-2026 (an acquisition not visible in the extracted data); tangible book and the ROTE cross-check should be re-checked against the Q2-26 10-Q note
Litigation / regulatory enforcement (1MDB precedent) and Apple Card partnership outcomes are not modelled as explicit charges

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketPrice) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 740.01-1153.99
data_sources.financials: research/GS/Reports/GS_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL-derived, 97 periods) for net income, equity, weighted diluted shares, SBC, DPS; SEC companyfacts API CIK 0000886982 (10-K FY2025 filed 2026-02-25, 10-Q Q2-2026 filed 2026-08-03) for net revenues (RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense), pre-tax earnings, income tax, net income to common, preferred dividends and stock, goodwill, intangibles, unsecured long-term debt, deposits, repurchases, dividends declared, common shares outstanding
data_sources.qualitative: research/GS/Reports/GS_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): segments, Q2-2026 results, FY2026 guidance (alternatives fundraising >$125bn, private credit $300bn by 2029, dividend $5.00 from Q3-26), Basel III March 2026 re-proposal, bull/bear cases
data_sources.method: .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing (bank -> residual income on tangible book), implemented as its FCFE clean-surplus equivalent on the component engine per the NAB.AX / IAG.AX / GL precedent

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E net revenues (GAAP 'net revenues' = total revenues less interest expense; XBRL us-gaap:RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported: FY0 = H1-2026 actual 37,565 (Q1 17,227 + Q2 20,338, 10-Q filed 2026-08-03) + H2-2026E 34,435, i.e. Q3/Q4 at ~17.2bn each -- back to the Q1-26 level and ~15% below the record Q2. H2-2025 was 28,638, so H2E is +20% YoY against H1's +27%. FY2025 actual 58,283; FY2024 53,512; FY2023 46,254; FY2022 47,365; FY2021 59,339 (prior peak); FY2020 44,560. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027 one year from the valuation date, which the engine's end-of-year discounting requires. The Metrics.csv has no Revenue column because build_facts_xbrl.py looks for us-gaap:Revenues, which GS does not tag; RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense is the series (same gap class as SOFI).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 Jun 2026: 291.44m common shares outstanding (us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding, Q2-26 10-Q; dei cover-page count 291.17m at 17 Jul 2026) PLUS ~11.5m RSUs and dilutive awards. Cross-check: Q2-26 weighted-average diluted shares 304.9m and basic 300.1m (GS's basic count already includes RSUs with no future service requirement) against a period-average common count of ~293m implies ~12m of RSUs/dilutives at the period end; 291.4 + 11.5 = 303m. Held FLAT: share-based compensation is expensed in the flows (it is inside compensation and benefits, hence inside the pre-tax margin), and buybacks are the DISTRIBUTION of the FCFE being valued, so projecting further shrinkage would count the same cash twice. FY2025 repurchases 12.36bn retired ~4% of the count; H1-2026 9.0bn.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. GS is a Fed-regulated bank holding company and G-SIB: unsecured long-term borrowings ($348.0bn at 30 Jun 2026, us-gaap:UnsecuredLongTermDebt), deposits ($558.0bn), short-term borrowings, repos and other secured financings are operating funding whose cost is already inside net revenues (which are stated net of interest expense). Cash and equivalents ($187.3bn) are held against that funding and the LCR, and are not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to hold CET1 as risk-weighted assets grow) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only. Preferred stock ($13.03bn carrying value at 30 Jun 2026) is a senior claim on that equity and IS deducted -- in equity_bridge, at carrying value, with the flows left pre-preferred-dividend (~0.9bn/yr; the two treatments are equivalent at par).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = FY2026E net income ~22,620 (H1 actual 12,258 + H2E ~10,360 at a 37.8% pre-tax margin and 20.5% tax) less capital retained ~1,080 (1.5% of net revenues, the model's floor). Actual H1-2026 retention was ~nil: common equity was 109,714 at 30 Jun 2026 vs 109,819 at 31 Dec 2025 while 9.0bn of buybacks, ~2.7bn of common dividends and 0.45bn of preferred dividends were paid -- GS distributed ~100% of earnings and let CET1 drift from ~15% toward ~14.5% as Basel III endgame requirements were recalibrated down (March 2026 re-proposal). reported_fcf = FCFE + SBC so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 -45,154; FY2024 -13,212; FY2023 -12,587; FY2021 +6,298) is trading-inventory, repo and loan-book movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column should not be read. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: 3,445 (FY2024 2,663; FY2023 2,085; FY2022 4,083; FY2021 2,348). H1-2026 2,969 is front-loaded (Q1 2,530: year-end awards to retirement-eligible employees are expensed at grant). Taxes paid on net-share settlement (kpis equity_award_taxes: FY2025 2,156; H1-2026 2,864) are NOT added: with SBC expensed at grant value and the count held flat, the withholding cash is economically a repurchase of the withheld shares, and charging it would double-count (see memory sbc-flat-share-count).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: net interest income ($13.6bn FY2025, $7.5bn H1-2026) IS part of the banking business and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: us-gaap:PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock FY2025 12,360 (FY2024 8,000; FY2023 5,796); H1-2026 9,000. Common dividends paid FY2025 ~4.4bn ($14.00/share declared: 3.00, 3.00, 4.00, 4.00); Q1 and Q2 2026 declared at $4.50 (us-gaap:CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared -- the Analysis JSON's '$4.00 to $5.00' is the July 2026 announcement of the Q3-26 rate; the H1-26 rate was $4.50). Buybacks are the FCFE distribution and are not a separate driver.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total shareholders' equity 122,742 at 30 Jun 2026 less preferred stock 13,028 = common equity 109,714; goodwill 7,342 + identifiable intangibles 1,929 = 9,271 (both stepped up in H1-2026 from 5,949 / 842 -- an acquisition; the Q2 10-Q note was not extracted) -> tangible common equity ~100,440. On ~298m period-end basic shares: BVPS ~$368, TBVPS ~$337 (derived, not the reported figures). ROTE: FY2025 16,300 / avg TCE ~99bn = ~16.5%; H1-2026 annualised ~23%; FY2023 ~8%. The market price is ~2.5x book and ~2.8x tangible book.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.25 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 10.45%, rounded to 10.5%. Beta 1.25 for a markets-facing G-SIB whose revenue is ~65% Global Banking & Markets (MQG.AX was set at 1.15, NAB.AX at 1.0). One rate across all three scenarios; cyclical, credit, regulatory and litigation risk is charged in the bear flows and in the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease cost sits inside occupancy / non-compensation expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin; lease liabilities are immaterial against $110bn of common equity. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: GS consolidates no material noncontrolling interests (no us-gaap:MinorityInterest tag in the filings); net income is attributable in full. Preferred dividends are the senior claim and are handled via the equity_bridge deduction of preferred stock at carrying value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (precedent NAB.AX 2026-09-24, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = TCE x g is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE)) and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. An owner-FCF DCF is invalid here: OCF is trading-book movement, deposits and unsecured debt are operating funding, and there is no EBITDA. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = net revenues (net of interest expense); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax margin (net revenues - compensation - non-compensation expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of net revenues, so that after the engine's SBC deduction EBIT = pre-tax earnings (FY2025 37.5% + 5.9% = 43.4%; FY2024 34.4%; FY2023 23.2%; FY2022 28.5%; FY2021 45.6%; FY2020 28.0%; H1-2026 40.1%); sbc_pct_path = 5.0% (FY2026E ~3,600 / 72,000; FY2021-25 average 5.6%); da_pct = 0 (depreciation and amortisation are inside non-compensation expense and are a real cost for a bank, not an add-back); lease_cost 0; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to hold CET1 as RWA grows with revenue = tangible common equity/net revenues (~1.4x at FY0, ~1.5x at mid-cycle revenue) x g, taken as 1.3 x g with a 1.5% floor because GS is running CET1 above the recalibrated requirement and its fee-heavy mix needs less capital per dollar of revenue than a lender (NAB was 2.6 x g); cash_tax_rate_path = 21.0% (FY2025 21.4%, FY2024 22.4%, FY2023 20.7%, H1-2026 18.5% on discrete items); wacc = cost of equity 10.5%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge deducts preferred stock 13,028. FY0 reconciliation: 72,000 x (44.0% - 5.0%) x (1 - 20.5%) = 22,320 vs FY2026E net income ~22,620 (H1 actual 12,258). MID-CYCLE: FY2026 is a record year (record Equities, record debt underwriting, IB fees +55% YoY in Q2) so the base path takes FY2027 net revenues DOWN 5% and holds the pre-tax margin at 33-34.5% -- the FY2019-25 average is 32.3% and the FY2024-26 average ~37% -- rather than compounding from the peak; the FY2021 -> FY2022 precedent was -20%. RESIDUAL-INCOME CROSS-CHECK on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (16.5 - 2.5)/(10.5 - 2.5) = 1.75x x ~$337 = ~$590/share at a mid-cycle 16.5% ROTE; the engine base should land modestly above that because FY2027-28 earnings sit above the mid-cycle run-rate. The market's ~2.8x TBV requires either a sustained ~22% ROTE or a cost of equity ~7.5%. Metrics.csv anchors used: NetIncome, ShareholdersEquity, SharesOutstanding (weighted diluted), StockBasedComp, DividendPerShare; the revenue, pre-tax, tax, preferred, goodwill/intangibles and debt series were read from the SEC companyfacts API (CIK 886982) because the Extracted/ folder is empty for this XBRL-only filer.

bear.growth_rationale: A 2022-23 style downturn: FY27 -15% (FY2022 was -20% from the FY2021 peak; softened for the larger AWM fee base), FY28 -5% as the AI-capex financing cycle and IPO window close together, then a slow recovery. FY2036 net revenues 73bn, roughly the FY2026E level: 2.1%/yr from FY2025.
bear.margin_rationale: Pre-tax 26% / 24% in FY27-28 (FY2023 was 23.2%, FY2022 28.5%): sticky non-comp expense and a comp floor against falling revenue, provisions rising on private-credit and card exposure. Recovers to 31% (FY2019-20 were 28-29%) as tougher final Basel III / FRTB rules keep the cost of balance-sheet-heavy trading revenue elevated.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention held at 3.0% in FY27-28 despite negative growth: in a downturn RWA migrates up and stress-capital buffers rise (2020 and 2008 precedents), so capital must be topped up while revenue falls; thereafter 1.3 x g.

base.growth_rationale: Net revenues. FY27 -5%: normalisation from a record year in which Equities (+72% YoY in Q2), debt underwriting and IB fees (+55%) all peaked together; milder than the FY2022 -20% because AWM management fees on ~$4.0tn of assets under supervision and financing revenue give a larger recurring base than in 2021. FY28 +1% (trough), then 4% as alternatives fundraising (>$125bn FY2026 target, private credit to $300bn by 2029) and financing compound, tapering to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less mature-market share drift). FY2036 net revenues 89.2bn: 3.9%/yr from FY2025, 2.8%/yr from the FY2021 peak.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin + SBC 5.0% on net revenues. FY27-28 33.0%: comp ratio drifts back to ~32.5% (FY2025 32.4%, H1-26 30.7% on record revenue) and non-comp expense (~18.6bn FY2025) is sticky in dollars, so a 5% revenue drop costs ~3pp of margin from FY2026E's ~39% (33 + 5 = 38.0). Mature 34.0-34.5%: mix shift toward AWM fees, Platform Solutions losses gone (GM card sold), provision ~1.2% of revenues (FY2024 2.5%, FY2025 a 1.9% release) -- above the FY2019-25 average of 32.3% but well below FY2021's 45.6% and H1-2026's 40.1%.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 as RWA grows with revenue = 1.3 x g with a 1.5% floor (tangible common equity ~1.4-1.5x net revenues, shaded for GS running above the recalibrated Basel III requirement and for a fee-heavy mix). At 4% growth 5.2% of revenues (~3.7bn, ~20% of net income retained -> ~80% distributed, which is the FY2023-25 pattern of ~6bn dividends + 6-12bn buybacks); at 2.5% terminal growth 3.3% (~13% retained). FY27-28 floored at 1.5% despite falling revenue: RWA migration and the final Basel rules mean capital is not released in a downturn.

bull.growth_rationale: Capital-markets upcycle persists (AI-infrastructure financing, M&A under a permissive antitrust regime), FY27 still grows 2% off the record base, then 5-6% as Goldman Sachs Alternatives ($500bn+), private credit ($300bn by 2029) and transaction/private banking compound. FY2036 net revenues 108bn: 5.8%/yr from FY2025.
bull.margin_rationale: Pre-tax 39-40% + SBC 5.0%: comp ratio ~30% held on operating leverage and AI cost-out, non-comp growing below revenue, provisions benign. FY2021 reached 45.6% and H1-2026 40.1%, so 40% sustained is a strong-but-seen level.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = 1.3 x g: faster growth needs more capital even at a higher ROTE (~22%). Terminal 3% growth retains ~12% of net income.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: the anchor year is a record on every line at once (Equities +72%, IB fees +55%, annualised ROTE 23%), the Analysis rates revenue cyclicality and recession sensitivity 'high', and the stock trades at ~2.8x tangible book -- a level from which the FY2021 -> FY2022 peak-to-trough repriced the shares by ~40%. Bull cut to 25%: it requires the AI-financing cycle, benign credit, a ~30% comp ratio and Basel relief to all hold for a decade, and the current price already discounts most of it.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
